title: Tom process definition (<id>.process.yaml)
description: A process: phases of steps (some grouping sub-steps), each phase ending with a quality-gate step and optionally a post-gate step whose todos are done before the next phase starts. Lives at _ai/processes/<id>/<id>.process.yaml beside <id>.md, the process description. Checked by validateProcessDefinition (src/utils/processDefinition.ts), which also enforces what a schema cannot: ids unique within their scope, maxIterations only with repeatable, onFail only on a gate and naming a step of its phase, a process listed at most once in a step's subprocesses / branches.

id.description: The process id; also its folder and file name.

summary.description: One line; the full description is the process's .md file.

session.description: The session every prompt of the process runs in unless a phase, step or sub-step names its own (the innermost applies). E.g. {name: tomspecs, mode: per-prompt, profile: opus-5-5-agent-sdk-mm}: every Proceed prompt starts fresh, without iteration placeholders in session names.

inputs.description: What the process takes when a step starts it (subprocesses: / branches:). Its prompts see each as ${input.<name>}.

kind.description: What it holds: a document, a list of documents, a folder.

required.description: An input the starting step must fill.

outputs.description: What it hands back to the step that started it as a subprocess, as ${sub.<process>.<name>}: set with tomAi_setProcessState {outputs}, or the default value.

kind.description: What it holds: a document, a list of documents, a folder.

required.description: An output that must be set before the process finishes as a subprocess.

value.description: The value when none was set: a text with ${input.<name>}, e.g. ${input.folder}/consolidated.md.

runParameters.description: The custom chat variables a run of this process keeps as its run parameters (e.g. `design`, `design-mode`). The PROCESS view's Reset Process (and tomAi_resetProcess with mode `process`) clears these and puts the run back to the process's first position.

prompt.description: What is to be done when it starts: the part of the prompt a process action (Next, Repeat, Gate passed, ...) adds for it.

role.description: The role doing it: a folder name under _ai/roles/.

userAction.description: Done by the user, not by an agent (reviewing, answering, approving): runs no prompt — no prompt or session allowed — and Proceed asks the user to confirm it is done. Not on a gate, nor on a step with sub-steps (flag the sub-steps); the validator enforces both.

subprocesses.description: The processes that may start from here as a subprocess: a level on the quest's process stack that hands a result back. A closed list: nothing else starts from this position. A sub-step without lists of its own takes its step's.

branches.description: The processes that may start from here as a branch: a level on the quest's process stack that hands nothing back. A closed list, like subprocesses.

prompt.description: What is to be done when it starts: the part of the prompt a process action (Next, Repeat, Gate passed, ...) adds for it.

role.description: The role doing it; with sub-steps, the role of those that name none.

optional.description: May be left out: the PROCESS view offers Leave out at its start, and leaving it out is recorded in the process state with its reason. Not on a gate (the validator refuses it there).

when.description: Runs only when this holds. Not on a gate (the validator refuses it there).

substeps.description: A step with sub-steps is no action of its own but a group of them.

userAction.description: Done by the user, not by an agent (reviewing, answering, approving): runs no prompt — no prompt or session allowed — and Proceed asks the user to confirm it is done. Not on a gate, nor on a step with sub-steps (flag the sub-steps); the validator enforces both.

onFail.description: Gate only: where a failed gate goes — the id of one of the phase's steps (or the gate's own id). Unset: the gate is run again. The validator refuses it on other steps and checks the id.

subprocesses.description: The processes that may start from here as a subprocess: a level on the quest's process stack that hands a result back. A closed list: nothing else starts from this position. A sub-step without lists of its own takes its step's.

branches.description: The processes that may start from here as a branch: a level on the quest's process stack that hands nothing back. A closed list, like subprocesses.

prompt.description: What is to be done when it starts: the part of the prompt a process action (Next, Repeat, Gate passed, ...) adds for it.

optional.description: May be left out: the PROCESS view offers Leave out at its start, and leaving it out is recorded in the process state with its reason. Not on a gate (the validator refuses it there).

when.description: Runs only when this holds. Not on a gate (the validator refuses it there).

todos.description: Todos done after the gate passed, before the next phase starts.

todoPrefix.description: Quest todos whose id starts with this prefix belong to the step too.

userAction.description: Done by the user, not by an agent (reviewing, answering, approving): runs no prompt — no prompt or session allowed — and Proceed asks the user to confirm it is done. Not on a gate, nor on a step with sub-steps (flag the sub-steps); the validator enforces both.

subprocesses.description: The processes that may start from here as a subprocess: a level on the quest's process stack that hands a result back. A closed list: nothing else starts from this position. A sub-step without lists of its own takes its step's.

branches.description: The processes that may start from here as a branch: a level on the quest's process stack that hands nothing back. A closed list, like subprocesses.

prompt.description: What is to be done when it starts: the part of the prompt a process action (Next, Repeat, Gate passed, ...) adds for it.

optional.description: May be left out: the PROCESS view offers Leave out at its start, and leaving it out is recorded in the process state with its reason. Not on a gate (the validator refuses it there).

when.description: Runs only when this holds. Not on a gate (the validator refuses it there).

gate.description: The quality gate that ends the phase.

postGate.description: Optional step after the gate passed.

session.description: The named session it runs in (a <name>.session.json of the quest's history folder); inherited from its step and phase when unset. A name, or the name with the session it is based on, its lifetime and its profile (so a missing session is created from the definition).

mode.description: The session's lifetime: continue (default), per-prompt (every prompt starts again, from the base or fresh), per-iteration (one conversation per queue iteration). fork-from-base is the old name of per-prompt.

profile.description: The Anthropic profile a missing session is created with (its prompts run with it unless the queue item names its own).

sessionName.description: A session name: letters, digits, "_" and "-"; ${phase-iteration}, ${step-iteration} and ${substep-iteration} are filled in, so every iteration gets its own session.

documents.description: The documents this position puts in front of the user (a review step's): the PROCESS view shows one link per document and the process tools name them. A sub-step without its own takes its step's.

path.description: Workspace-relative (or absolute) path; placeholders: ${<chat variable>} (e.g. ${idea-document}, ${quest}), ${input.<name>}, ${output.<name>}, ${dirname:<variable>} (the folder of a path a variable holds). A .md file opens in the MD Browser, a .process.yaml under _ai/processes/ in the process editor, any other file in its default editor.

label.description: What the link says; default: the file name.

processList.description: Process ids, or {process, description}; each process at most once.

description.description: Why or when to start it (shown where it is offered).

inputs.description: The process's declared inputs filled from this position: input name → a text the placeholder engine resolves when the level starts (the step's chat and process variables, ${sub.<process>.<name>}).

condition.description: When a phase or step runs. The key says who decides: `{var, equals | notEquals | in | set}` is decided by the extension from the chat variables (a custom one by its name, `custom.<name>`, the built-ins, `input.<name>` of a nested level) — a forward move passes a phase or step whose test fails by and records it; a variable that is not set decides nothing except `set`, and the agent judges it. `{judge: text}` is judged by the agent at Proceed, which leaves the phase or step out with tomAi_setProcessState {leaveOut: why} when it does not hold.

set.description: true: runs when the variable has a value; false: when it has none.

judge.description: The condition, as text the agent judges at Proceed.

followUps.description: Follow-up processes (vscimpb47): where the quest may continue when this level ends — another process (or this one) at a named phase and step, the first ones by default. Offered as an option of the decision at the end of the level (a step with follow-ups ends at a decision; the process's at the end of its last phase); the user picks it, the position switches there in the same run, its chat variables kept, and the switch is recorded (state `origins`, the decisions journal). The validator checks that the process, phase and step exist.

process.description: The process to continue in (its id under _ai/processes/).

phase.description: The phase to continue at; default the process's first phase.

step.description: The step of that phase to continue at (with phase); default its first step.

description.description: Shown with the option: what continuing there is for.

carry.description: The chat variables the follow-up relies on; their values are recorded with the switch (the run's chat variables stay as they are).

context.description: The call context: name → text, resolved by the placeholder engine when the switch is made (file names, comments); the follow-up's prompts read each as ${origin.<name>}, and ${process-origin} names where it came from.
